newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold plans Harmony refinery.
newsitem.headline: Randgold plans Harmony refinery.

text.p: South African mining house Randgold said on Monday trials at a pilot gold refinery on its Harmony site had been successfully completed and it is to begin designing a commercial-scale plant.
The six-week trial saw the pilot plant produce 86 kg of 99.99 percent pure gold and met all expectations, Harmony managing director Bernard Swanepoel said in a statement.
Plans for the larger plant are to be drawn up by technology supplier Mintek.
"The company will make a final decision on whether to proceed with the comercial refinery when it has reviewed Mintek's detailed proposals next month," the firm said.
The planned refinery will have a capacity of two tonnes of gold a month, equal to the Harmony mine's normal output, and could be up and running by the second half of 1997.
The cost of the plant will be around three million rand, but the project is aimed at reaping material cost savings.
